title: Preparing your home for a patient coming back from hospital
description: Simple steps to make your home safer and more comfortable for a patient's first days after hospital discharge.
image_alt: Nurse helping an elderly patient at home
body:
A patient's first days at home after hospital need a little preparation that makes a big difference to comfort and safety. Here are the key steps:

## Set up a comfortable, close space
- Keep the patient's room as close to the bathroom as possible.
- Make sure there is enough light, especially in hallways at night.
- Keep what they need (water, phone, glasses) within easy reach.

## Reduce the risk of falls
- Remove small rugs and cables from walkways.
- Use a non-slip mat in the bathroom.
- Ask the doctor or physiotherapist whether the patient needs a cane, walker or bathroom grab bars.

## Organise medications
- Write a medication schedule exactly as the doctor prescribed.
- Use a pill organiser by day if it suits you.
- Never change a dose without checking with the doctor.

## Keep contact numbers ready
Post a list with the treating doctor, the hospital, emergency services and the family member following the case.

> This information is general. Always follow the treating doctor's instructions and the hospital discharge plan.

If you need someone to follow up with the patient at home after surgery or hospital discharge, the **Dar Alamana** team is here to help.
